clue.text: Undergoes instruction, delaying one politician's passing

indicators.note: delaying the one means its letter turns up later in the word than it normally would

parts.note: someone who undergoes instruction trains
one is the Roman numeral I
a Tory is a British Conservative politician; the 's is just possessive

explanation.surface: Someone studying puts off a politician's departure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delaying one' shifts the I in TRAINS to later, giving TRANSI.
explanation.definitionFit: Something passing lasts only briefly, which is exactly what transitory describes.

clue.text: It takes nearly thirty-one days to get this brandy

indicators.note: nearly means stopping just short, so the final letter of the month is dropped

parts.note: March is a month with thirty-one days

explanation.surface: A brandy that supposedly takes about a month to make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' removes the last letter, H, from MARCH. Marc is a brandy distilled from grape pressings.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc is a type of brandy made from the skins and pips left after winemaking.

clue.text: Perimeters of lodge accommodating ancient Greek screen

indicators.note: accommodating means holding something inside, so one piece goes within the other
the perimeters of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: Attic is the ancient Greek dialect of Athens, so an ancient Greek can be Attic

explanation.surface: A lodge's surroundings house an old Greek screen.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer letters of lodge, L and E, go around ATTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice is a criss-cross framework often used as a decorative screen.

clue.text: Commander marks defile in mountain range

parts.note: CO stands for commanding officer
M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency
a defile or narrow route through mountains is a pass

explanation.surface: A commanding officer notes a gorge among the peaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mountain range' looks like one phrase, but 'mountain' belongs with 'defile' and 'range' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass can mean scope or extent, the same as a range of something.

clue.text: Woman who carves busts plus crests?

indicators.note: busts as a verb means breaks, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A female sculptor producing busts as well as heraldic crests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busts' reads as the noun for sculpted heads, but it is a verb signalling the anagram of PLUS CRESTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sculptress is a female sculptor, one who carves stone or wood.

clue.text: A turn in the past

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: A turn taken some time ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Ago describes something having happened before now, back in time.

clue.text: Have resounding effect, City hero raving about it

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the anagram goes around the other piece
raving means wild or mad, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: A football club's star wildly celebrating has a big impact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raving' turns HERO into RE HO, which goes 'about' EC; 'it' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-echo is to sound again and again, so it has a resounding effect.

clue.text: Expert given right to shout from the housetops

parts.note: a pro is an expert or professional
a claim is a right to something

explanation.surface: A professional is given the right to shout loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: To shout from the housetops is to announce something publicly, which is to declare it loudly.

clue.text: Intellectual argument introduced by Anglo-Catholic bishop?

indicators.note: introduced by means the argument comes after the other pieces

parts.note: Anglo-Catholics belong to the High Church wing of Anglicanism
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a row is an argument

explanation.surface: A row started by a High Church bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A highbrow is a person of refined intellectual tastes.

clue.text: Collected tartan cloth worn by head of clan

indicators.note: worn by means the head of clan is placed inside the cloth

parts.note: plaid is tartan cloth

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A clan chief dressed in tartan.
explanation.walkthrough: The C from clan goes inside PLAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Collected in the sense of calm and composed, meaning untroubled.

clue.text: Newspaper backed by British seamen once or students?

indicators.note: backed means turned round, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: NUS was the National Union of Seamen, and is also the National Union of Students

explanation.surface: A newspaper supported by sailors or students.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid daily.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun is a well-known British tabloid daily paper.

clue.text: Spirit from Greek island, quietly taken back (present)

indicators.note: taken back means moved to the rear, so the soft letter goes to the end

parts.note: Patmos is a Greek island in the Aegean
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly
here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: A Greek island's spirit, quietly recalled as still present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken back' moves P to the end of PATMOS, giving ATMOSP.
explanation.definitionFit: Atmosphere can mean the prevailing mood or spirit of a place.

clue.text: "Are you the vicar? Come again"

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a vicar's title
asking 'is it ...?' is a way of asking 'are you ...?' on the phone or at a door

explanation.surface: Someone at the door asks whether the caller is the vicar, and invites a return visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are you the vicar?' is rephrased as 'Rev, is it?'.
explanation.definitionFit: To revisit is to come back again to a place.

clue.text: Cake flavouring is a requirement on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside means the need goes around the other word

parts.note: a need is a requirement

explanation.surface: A cake's flavour is what's needed on its outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the outside' tells you the requirement wraps around 'is'; the opening 'a' stands as itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Aniseed is a liquorice-tasting seed used to flavour cakes and sweets.

clue.text: Feline connections, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: links are connections

explanation.surface: Cats seem to have some connections.
explanation.definitionFit: The lynx is a wild cat, so it is a feline.

clue.text: Sparkling individual initially reflecting Irish ancestry

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the word
reflecting means mirrored, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: descent is ancestry or lineage

explanation.surface: A sparkling personality shows off Irish roots.
explanation.definitionFit: Iridescent means shimmering with changing colours, so glittering or sparkling.

clue.text: Get involved in farming — there may be money in it

definitions.meaning: to work the soil on a farm

definitions.text: there may be money in it

explanation.definitionFit: Till means both to cultivate land and a shop's cash drawer, matching the two halves.

clue.text: Possibly the thing — though it may not be definite

definitions.text: Possibly the thing — though it may not be definite

parts.words: Possibly the thing — though it may not be definite
parts.note: a word like 'the' is a definite grammatical part of speech, a thing is an item, and 'a' is the indefinite kind

explanation.definitionFit: An article is a thing or item, and in grammar 'the' is the definite one while 'a' is indefinite.

clue.text: Give the game away, making one's pulse drop?

definitions.meaning: pulses are edible seeds such as beans, so letting them fall is a literal reading

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means revealing a secret, and literally means letting legumes fall out.

clue.text: Attempt when fencing to take in agreement

indicators.note: fencing means enclosing, so the attempt surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a try is an attempt
to eat is to take in food

explanation.surface: A fencer's attempt to reach an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between states.

clue.text: Propulsion of missiles tested at first in part of garden

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the garden feature

parts.note: a rockery is a garden feature of stones and plants

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Missiles tested first in a garden corner.
explanation.walkthrough: A ROCKERY is a common British garden feature of rocks and alpine plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocketry is the science of rocket propulsion for missiles and spacecraft.

clue.text: A graduate supporting a dog briefly in the Birmingham area?

indicators.note: in a down answer, supporting means placed underneath

parts.note: lab is short for Labrador, a dog
an MA is a Master of Arts graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate holds up a dog around Birmingham.
explanation.walkthrough: Birmingham is a city in this US state, not only the English one.
explanation.definitionFit: Birmingham is the largest city in the US state of Alabama, so this is its area.

clue.text: New ad must come, produced to order

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh advert must arrive, made to order.
explanation.definitionFit: Custom-made goods are produced to a particular customer's order.

clue.text: Cats, possibly, wrongly presented as rich game?

parts.note: Cats is an example of a stage musical

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A musical about felines is misrepresented as a lavish game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presented' is just a link; 'wrongly' rearranges AS RICH.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a party game where players scramble for seats when the music stops.

clue.text: Sort of music exam taken outside city (one English abandoned)

indicators.note: taken outside means the exam goes around the city

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam

indicators.note: abandoned means the letter is left out

parts.note: Chester is an English cathedral city
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An exam held outside a city, with one English person leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' drops just one of the city's two Es, and 'taken outside' wraps the exam around what remains. CHESTER is a cathedral city in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchestral describes music written for or played by an orchestra.

clue.text: One who substitutes for a traveller of some standing, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: to commute is to exchange or substitute one thing for another

definitions.text: a traveller of some standing, perhaps
definitions.meaning: someone travelling daily to work, often standing on a crowded train

explanation.definitionFit: A commuter travels regularly to work, and literally is one who exchanges one thing for another.

clue.text: Swiss providing information on Welsh fellow

parts.note: gen is slang for information
Evan is a typical Welsh man's name

explanation.surface: A Swiss man passes on details about a Welshman.
explanation.definitionFit: A Genevan is someone from Geneva, a Swiss city.

clue.text: Funeral procession's time, say, to appear in centre

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: to appear in means the pieces are placed inside

parts.note: the core is the centre
eg means for example, which is what say means

explanation.surface: It's time for the funeral cortege to appear in the town centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A cortege is a solemn procession, especially at a funeral.

clue.text: Current light enveloping small detached territory

indicators.note: enveloping means wrapping around another piece

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
to light is to land, as a bird alights

explanation.surface: A current light surrounds a small place.
explanation.definitionFit: An island is land cut off by water, hence a detached territory.

clue.text: Democrat in formal wear going up to amend copy

indicators.note: going up in a down answer means reading from bottom to top
in means the Democrat goes inside the tie

parts.note: a tie, as in white tie, is formal wear

explanation.surface: A Democrat in a dinner jacket rises to correct the text.
explanation.walkthrough: D inside TIE gives TIDE, which 'going up' turns around.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit is to revise or correct written material.
